reasoning: Designed. Latent values for Lender Spreads, Chip Lead Times and Bitcoin Hashprice are mapped from this scenario's own market path (public quantities); Revenue Gap, Grid Reserve Margin and Efficiency Index are authored. Displayed values add observation noise; the sharp range brackets the latent value.
DO_NOT_EXPOSE: authoring_latent must never be read by bots, the UI, or 'Read the market'. Runtime reads only series[].displayed, .arrow and .sharp.
neutral_tolerance: +-12 (structural drift: halving, efficiency trend, grid retirements)

trigger.title: The Digestion Quarter
trigger.narrative: In April 2028, just as the fifth halving lands, two of the four biggest cloud buyers tell investors they will 'digest' capacity already contracted and pause new leasing for a quarter. Nothing breaks: no tenant defaults and no lender leaves. But H100 and Blackwell rents fall 12-15% in a quarter, hyperscale cap rates back up about 45 bp, AI-infrastructure multiples lose roughly three turns and the AI demand index dips from 94 to 86. It proves to be a price reset rather than a crisis: rents stabilise within three quarters, and renewals on the calendar now price 20-30% below 2025 levels for good.

effects.recovery: rents flat by 2028Q4; cap rates back to 5.85% by 2028Q4; multiples recovered by 2029Q1

decoy.reason: A mid-size private-credit fund gates redemptions after a bad quarter in unrelated (software and consumer) loans. GPU-backed lenders pause new drawdowns for a few weeks and reprice the whole desk +100-225 bp. Tenant credit is unchanged and every existing contract keeps paying.
decoy.tell: Tenant CDS and lab revenue are flat while spreads spike; the move reverses within two quarters once the fund's redemptions are met. The card 'The Private Credit Wobble' names the cause.
decoy.fair_in_hindsight: The spread move was real and the same tool (lender repricing) later carries S1's trigger. But it arrived without any widening in the Revenue Gap, without a weaker hashprice, and with tenants still paying.
